title: Another Storm Heads to Hawaii!
summary:
Hawaii is getting hit again! Just a week after Hurricane Lala caused big floods, another storm is coming. It's called Tropical Storm Moke. It's bringing more rain and strong winds.

The storm is passing south of the islands, so it won't hit directly. But it could drop up to 15 inches of rain on the Big Island. That's a lot of water! It could cause more flooding and mudslides.

Last week, Hurricane Lala dropped more than 30 inches of rain in some places. That caused floods that swept through towns and lifted homes off their foundations. Roads and bridges were destroyed. More than 8,000 people still don't have power. One 90-year-old woman died in the flood.

Now, people are getting ready for more bad weather. The governor of Hawaii, Josh Green, asked the White House to declare an emergency. The mayor of Hawaii County, Kimo Alameda, told people to prepare for power outages and hazardous roads.

So, if you live in Hawaii, you need to be careful. And if you're watching from far away, you can hope that everyone stays safe. This is a reminder that nature can be really powerful.
why_it_matters: Learning about storms can help you understand why your family might make an emergency plan or kit, and why safety warnings during bad weather are so important.

background_read: Hawaii is a chain of islands in the Pacific Ocean and part of the United States.
The Big Island is the largest island in Hawaii, and it can get very heavy rain during storms.
When a state has a dangerous emergency, its governor can ask the national government to declare an emergency so help can arrive faster.
Article_Structure: WHO: People in Hawaii, Governor Josh Green, and Mayor Kimo Alameda.
WHAT: Another storm called Tropical Storm Moke is bringing more rain and wind just a week after Hurricane Lala.
WHERE: Hawaii, especially the Big Island, with the storm passing south of the islands.
WHY: The heavy rain could cause more flooding and mudslides on top of damage from last week.

perspectives.description: They are worried about more flooding and damage after last week's hurricane, and many are still without power.
They are telling people to get ready for power outages and dangerous roads, and they asked for an emergency declaration.
They are hoping everyone in Hawaii stays safe and may want to help in some way.
